back: Applying oint B.dl = mu_0 i to a loop around a charging capacitor's wire gives B ≠ 0, but a pot/tiffin-shaped surface with the same rim touches no current, giving zero. Maxwell resolved this by introducing the displacement current.
i_d = epsilon_0 dPhi_E/dt. Arises from a time-varying electric field, not from flow of charges. Has the same magnetic effects as a conduction current.

front: Inside vs outside a charging capacitor
back: Outside the plates: only conduction current (i_c = i, i_d = 0). Inside: only displacement current (i_c = 0, i_d = i). Total current i is the same everywhere: i = i_c + i_d.
oint B.dl = mu_0 (i_c + epsilon_0 dPhi_E/dt). Ampere's law generalised to include the displacement current. Its symmetry with Faraday's law is the basis of EM waves.

front: The four Maxwell's equations in vacuum
back: (1) oint E.dA = Q/epsilon_0 (Gauss electricity); (2) oint B.dA = 0 (Gauss magnetism); (3) oint E.dl = -dPhi_B/dt (Faraday); (4) oint B.dl = mu_0(i_c + epsilon_0 dPhi_E/dt) (Ampere-Maxwell).
Only accelerated charges radiate EM waves. Stationary charges and uniform-motion (steady current) charges do not. An oscillating charge radiates a wave of the same frequency.

front: Why light frequency couldn't be tested first
back: Yellow light oscillates at about 6 x 10^14 Hz, while electronic circuits barely reach 10^11 Hz. Hence Hertz's experimental demonstration came in the radio-wave region (1887).

Maxwell predicted EM waves (light is an EM wave). Hertz (1887) first produced radio waves. J.C. Bose (Kolkata) produced 25 mm - 5 mm waves. Marconi transmitted over many km - beginning of radio communication.
E and B are perpendicular to each other and to the direction of propagation. Self-sustaining oscillations in vacuum - no material medium required. The direction of propagation is E x B.
E_x = E_0 sin(kz - omega t); B_y = B_0 sin(kz - omega t). k = 2pi/lambda (wave number), omega = angular frequency, wave vector k gives direction of propagation.

front: Speed of EM waves in vacuum
back: c = 1/sqrt(mu_0 epsilon_0) = 3 x 10^8 m/s. Equivalent relations: omega = ck and nu lambda = c. c is the same for all wavelengths, hence used to define a standard of length.

front: EM waves in a material medium
back: v = 1/sqrt(mu epsilon), where epsilon and mu are the permittivity and permeability of the medium. The ratio of speeds in two media defines the refractive index.

front: Relation between E and B amplitudes
back: B_0 = E_0/c, or E_0 = c B_0. Example: for E = 6.3 V/m, B = E/c = 2.1 x 10^-8 T.
Produced by accelerated motion of charges in conducting wires. Range 500 kHz - 1000 MHz. AM: 530-1710 kHz. Short wave: up to 54 MHz. TV: 54-890 MHz. FM: 88-108 MHz. Cellular phones use UHF.
GHz-range short-wavelength radio waves, produced by klystrons, magnetrons and Gunn diodes. Used in radar, speed guns, and microwave ovens (frequency matched to the water molecule resonance).

Produced by hot bodies and molecules. Called heat waves because water molecules absorb them, increasing thermal motion. Key role in the greenhouse effect. Used in IR lamps, satellites, and LED remote switches.

Incoming visible light passes through the atmosphere, is absorbed by the Earth's surface, and re-radiated as infrared. Greenhouse gases (CO2, water vapour) trap this longer-wavelength radiation, keeping Earth warm.
The portion detected by the human eye: 4 x 10^14 Hz to 7 x 10^14 Hz, i.e. 700-400 nm. Snakes detect infrared; many insects' visible range extends into ultraviolet.

400 nm down to 0.6 nm. Produced by special lamps and the Sun; most absorbed by the ozone layer (40-50 km). Causes tanning; absorbed by glass; used in LASIK and to kill germs in water purifiers. CFCs deplete the ozone layer.
10 nm down to 10^-4 nm. Generated by bombarding a metal target with high-energy electrons. Diagnostic tool and treatment for certain cancers. Care needed - damages living tissue.
10^-10 m to less than 10^-14 m, the highest frequencies. Produced in nuclear reactions and emitted by radioactive nuclei. Used in medicine to destroy cancer cells.
The classification of EM waves by frequency is based roughly on how they are produced and/or detected; there are no sharply defined boundaries between the bands.
